name: mesh-code-mcp
instructions:
══ MESH CODE — MANDATORY SESSION RULES ══

This room is a shared workspace. One or more teammates (human or AI) may be
editing simultaneously on other machines. You MUST use Mesh Code tools to
stay in sync. Failing to do so causes duplicated work, overwritten changes,
and repeated mistakes your teammates already learned from.

NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES:

1. FIRST ACTION EVERY TURN: call `mesh.sync_room`. Do this BEFORE reading
   any file, running any command, or answering the user. The response tells
   you what changed since you last looked. Skipping this means you are
   working with stale state.

2. FIRST TIME IN THIS CONVERSATION: also call `mesh.get_resume_packet` to
   bootstrap context. It returns a compact 1,500-token packet covering the
   feature card, blockers, failed attempts, and the next action.

3. AFTER EVERY MEANINGFUL ACTION (file edit, test run, tool call, decision,
   hypothesis, error, blocker, resolution): call `mesh.log_action` with a
   one-line summary. Pick a specific event_type from the enum if the
   default `action.edit` is wrong. This is how teammates see your work.

4. BEFORE TOUCHING A FEATURE ANOTHER AGENT IS WORKING: call
   `mesh.get_feature_card` first. If they have an active claim, either
   coordinate via `mesh.log_action` or call `mesh.claim_task` to take over.

5. ON PAUSE OR HANDOFF: call `mesh.write_checkpoint` with `next_action` in
   plain English. The next agent (maybe on a different machine with a
   different model) reads this first and continues without restating.

WHEN A USER ASKS "what is X working on" OR "what happened":
   Always use `mesh.sync_room` and/or `mesh.search_history`. Do not guess
   from local files — the answer lives in the shared ledger.

Your identity (actor_id, session_id, device, agent_kind) is auto-detected
and merged into every tool call. You do not need to include them in args.
Room id is set via MESH_ROOM_ID in your MCP config.

══════════════════════════════════════════
